name: Orbit AI - Phase 2 - Missed Follow-up check (05 Section 3, new - not brief-W-numbered)

nodes.name: Every hour
nodes.notes: 05 Section 3: 'Missed Follow-up detection: one unified rule - any scheduled touch overdue without disposition fires an alert.' Hourly, not daily - a missed callback or demo matters within the hour, not the next morning. Confirm the instance's configured timezone, same caveat every scheduleTrigger in this repo carries.

nodes.name: Fetch ScheduledTouches
nodes.notes: Fetches the whole table rather than a filtered query - Twenty CRM's REST filter support for 'disposition IS NULL' isn't confirmed, and this table is expected to stay small (only future/recent touches, not permanent history), so a client-side filter is the safer bet over guessing a null-check filter syntax that might silently return zero rows.

nodes.name: Filter overdue, undispositioned
nodes.notes: Returns one item per overdue touch (not a single aggregate item) - 'any scheduled touch... fires an alert' reads as per-touch, not a batched summary, so the next Alert node fires once per row.

nodes.name: Alert: Missed Follow-up

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ severity: 'warning', source: 'missed-follow-up-check', message: 'Missed Follow-up: ' + $json.eventType + ' scheduled ' + $json.scheduledAt + ' for ' + $json.subjectType + ' ' + $json.subjectId + ' has no disposition.', linkUrl: ($env.TWENTY_CRM_BASE_URL || '') + '/objects/' + $json.subjectType + '/' + $json.subjectId }) }}

nodes.notes: 'Missed Follow-up' is its own named channel in 05 Section 14 (#missed-follow-ups) - alertRouting.ts's channelForSource already routes any source containing 'missed-follow-up' there, so this lands correctly with no extra wiring needed on the Command Center side.
